stats.title: Stats & forecast
stats.progressHint: Light bar: words in your deck. Dark bar: words reviewed at least once. The denominator is that level’s word count in the pack.
stats.otherCards: {{n}} other cards (unlevelled words, or words no longer in the current pack)
stats.forecastHint: Drag to choose new words per day. The load is SIMULATED by running FSRS-6 itself — the same engine that schedules your reviews — not a rule of thumb.
stats.loadLine: At steady state (~1 year in): about {{reviews}} reviews/day ≈ {{minutes}} min/day.
stats.secsMeasured: ({{s}} s/card — measured from your own review history)
stats.secsDefault: ({{s}} s/card — default; your own history takes over after 50 reviews)
stats.simNote: This forecasts VOCABULARY COVERAGE (words in your deck), not proficiency. Listening, speaking and grammar take their own time.
stats.anchorsHint: These anchors assume an ENGLISH-speaking learner. For a Vietnamese speaker Mandarin is substantially cheaper: tones are native equipment and ~60% of Vietnamese vocabulary is Sino-Vietnamese (the 大学→đại học pairs on your cards). Read 2,200 h as a CEILING, not a price.
stats.anchorCefr: CEFR (Cambridge guided learning hours): A2 ≈ 180–200h · B1 ≈ 350–400h · B2 ≈ 500–600h · C1 ≈ 700–800h · C2 ≈ 1,000–1,200h
stats.anchorFsiFr: FSI — French: ~600–750 class hours to professional working proficiency
stats.anchorFsiZh: FSI — Mandarin: ~2,200 hours for an English speaker — for a Vietnamese speaker this is an upper bound
stats.anchorsCredit: Sources: Cambridge English (guided learning hours) · FSI, US State Department (public domain).
